column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3a precedent; Missouri's 'Since March 1990' and maturities quote verified at source (rater P), but the idea (a lottery buys a Treasury per dated prize) is Q16-018's; add the 35 years there; name the practice, never the STRIPS instrument.

Mon 16 Nov: Figure 1 total row; $34,904,000 maturity value = Total installment payments due 34,904,000 verified at source (rater P); precedent for a total row Figure 1 already has; face against face, while Figure 1's printed rows foot $1 off 8h's totals.

Mon 16 Nov: Table 1 and 2.5 bridge; verified (liability at present value $28,716,413 against fair value $26,368,763); say the negative restricted position was presented as unrestricted net position; one bridging sentence only, Section 2 has about 46 words spare.
Mon 16 Nov: store, 3a or Table 3 reserve check; FY2025 cash flows show proceeds 3,752,000 and payments (3,752,000), verified at source (rater P); $42,180 to $50,000 matches 8h.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 or 3a evidence; even a lottery holding a bond per prize prints bonds and prizes in two tables that cannot be paired, which is why Table 1's Pays for column and Figure 1's rows matter; design evidence, never a boast in prose.
Mon 16 Nov: the same matched-maturity policy in words as Q16-018 and Q16-019; 'eliminating interest rate risk' is true only held to the end, as for Laura.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a or 3e plain sentence for a rate rise (the price moves, what each Treasury pays on its date does not); MD&A read at source, notes not; sits beside store Q17-021.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; UNVERIFIED (search extract); one value basis per column, which Figure 1 and Table 1 already name; read the Illinois note at source before any use.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a and Table 3: US public plans test every year whether each projected payment is covered, a sentence plus a year-by-year table, as Figure 1 would be re-run each January; assets at an assumed 7%, so never like for like.
Mon 16 Nov: Figure 1 heads; second precedent for the arithmetic in the head and for the rounding line, which Figure 1 needs since its rows foot to $444,081 and $55,919; row 11 is the closer shape.

Mon 16 Nov: Figure 1 clarity (panel 2 at 3): the closest professional shape for its right half with the formula in the head; borrow the formula, never the Funded and Unfunded labels (the extra Treasuries are owned, and unfunded reads as short).

Mon 16 Nov: Figure 1 option; the zeros column was seen only in a search extract (p. 33 at source), so partly verified; a second precedent for DESIGNS section 8's $0 column (Q14a-014) if the today's-rates world stays.
Mon 16 Nov: Figure 1 title or 3a first sentence; OPERS page 1 and page 5 N/A lines verified at source (rater P); evidence for row 37's verdict line, said in words, never N/A.
Mon 16 Nov: guard for Figure 1 and Table 3: never draw the reserve's balance and the yearly $50,000 on one scale; chart image not seen.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a headline candidate; about 89% is Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS (88.8%): say $444,080 of the $500,000 or add the ratio to 8h first; never set beside BTPS's 70% as like for like (credit and uncertain liabilities).

Mon 16 Nov: Figure 1 title; the built title already ends with if cash waiting earns nothing, so the change is to put the condition first, not to add it; fix the use cell's claim that it sits over the columns only.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; printed figures beside the marks, which Figure 1 already does; images not seen.
Mon 16 Nov: Figure 1 clarity, small: say once that 2033 means the payment due 1 Jan 2033 whose cash arrives 20 to 22 Dec 2032 (8h); a few words in the head or note.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the built Extra Treasuries column already names the gap's source; $35,894 is their January 2028 cost while the column pays $55,920, so never one figure for both.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e beside the store's Q3b rows (no one can force a sale); the forced-seller warning is common pension practice.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; members are not judges; serves no part.
Mon 16 Nov: 2.5 or 3a: value-matching (a hedge ratio) is a weaker claim than paying each payment on its date; say the cash match positively, never not duration-matched against TNA l.7.
Mon 16 Nov: UNVERIFIED (search extract); the two totals idea is Q14b-015's, here from a Dutch pension fund.
Mon 16 Nov: the same hedge-ratio contrast as row 22; ABP read at source, Campina UNVERIFIED.

Mon 16 Nov: 3a aha; verified at source (PRA Rulebook and Bank of England, rater P): surpluses and shortfalls accumulate at the risk-free rate and the highest accumulated shortfall may reach 3% of the liabilities' present value; say stricter on these two counts only (insurers also run Tests 2 and 3), a test, not a forecast.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the regulator receives one figure per test, support for a one-line headline beside Figure 1.
Mon 16 Nov: store; an annuity insurer publishes the match in words only (first 100,000 characters read); a quiet point at most, never a boast.
Mon 16 Nov: UNVERIFIED (search extracts); the same words-only point as row 27.
Mon 16 Nov: store; UNVERIFIED (search extract); Treasuries need no default cut and may be called guaranteed (Book 19); verify before any use.
Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; pledge schedules are dates and amounts with a donor behind them but no named asset; never say nothing is behind them.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d store; the 10% allowance and the buckets are new, but needing no allowance is the recipient's judgement, not an accounting rule: say Laura's figure is owned before it is stated (Q7c-035), and her ten payments are never offered to co-sponsors (SKELETON 3d).
Mon 16 Nov: store; even a large funder shows commitments with no matched source; one clause at most for 3d.
Mon 16 Nov: reserve design only if 3a ever draws dollars; DESIGNS keeps the numbers printed and the black tick means 1 January.
Mon 16 Nov: design evidence to keep Figure 1's row-per-payment form; 28 documents, several only as extracts, not a census; never said in prose as Figure 1 beating professionals.

Mon 16 Nov: Figure 1 clarity (panel 2 at 3; fresh reader read the $50,000 column twice): one world per exhibit, today's rates to the note with $74,123 and $45,456 (8h); reopens the spec's call to keep the column, so pair it with row 37's title and find words in a full 60-word note.

Mon 16 Nov: Figure 1 clarity, the cheapest fix: the sum in the head, Its own Treasury + Extra Treasuries = $50,000, and a footed total; 8h's $444,080 and $55,920 are unrounded totals, the printed rows foot to $444,081 and $55,919, so keep the rounding clause.

Mon 16 Nov: Figure 1 clarity, condition first then the verdict; about 89% is not in NUMBERS (say $444,080 of $500,000 or add it to 8h); no payment short is true by design, not a test result; keep the title to two lines (Section 3 has no headroom).

Mon 16 Nov: Table 1 and 2.5: one sentence bridges cost to payout (Missouri's matched book reads short on market value); both built titles already carry their scale ($300,000; $450,000), so only the bridge is new.
Mon 16 Nov: 3a or Figure 1 note: the gap grows from $2,662 (2033) to $7,820 (2041), $7,531 in 2042 (8h); the reason is Keel's reading; say interest, never coupons, in prose; the note has no room.
